column2: The S.T.R.O.N.G ActHistorically,11.5 percent or less of the ASUC elected positions are composed of students who transferred to UC Berkeley,despite this demographic making up nearly 30 percent of the incoming class. This act would further bridge the unequal representation in the ASUC by elevating the position of ‘Transfer Student Representative’ to an Executive Officer in order to better align with the scope of their responsibilities,and the proportion of the student body which they represent. This would ensure that the transfer student narrative is sufficiently present within the student government’s executive body and campus administration. View full proposed changeshere.Do you approve of this act to amend the ASUC Constitution?
column4: Save Free Student Press The Daily Californian is UC Berkeley’s student paper,bringing campus and city news to our community since 1871. The Daily Cal is financially independent from the University,UC Berkeley and ASUC,allowing it to report on these bodies without fear of retaliation. As Berkeley’s newspaper of record,the Daily Cal gives opportunities to future generations of journalists and businesspeople. The paper is currently supported by UC Berkeley undergraduate and graduate students through a $6.50 semesterly and $2.50 summer fee. This,however,will terminate in spring 2027. In order to keep producing consistent and hard-hitting news about UC Berkeley,and to continue to support the paper’s weekly print and distribution across the campus and city,the publication is presenting the Save Free Student Press initiative,a $8.50 per semester fee and $4 summer fee,adjusted to account for growing costs of business operations and declining ad revenue. The new fee will begin in fall 2027 and run till summer 2032. Supporting the student press is a crucial part holding campus and the administration accountable,while also creating opportunities for all UC Berkeley students pursuing journalism.Do you approve this fee?
column6: GA Fee 2.0The Graduate Assembly (GA) at UC Berkeley supports graduate and professional students through opportunities in employment,advocacy,campus committee representation,graduate registered student organization (GRSO) funding,scholarships and grants for underrepresented and/or marginalized students,and various other initiatives. This referendum will increase the GA Fee to promote the GA’s capacity to perform these functions for the graduate and professional community. Fee Start: Fall 2026 Fee Sunset (unless extended by subsequent referenda): Spring 2033 Fee Amount: $43.00 per semester (Fall and Spring only) Return-to-Aid: $14.33 per semester (33.3%) Paid by: All UC Berkeley graduate students,academic and professional,including students in self-sustaining graduate and professional degree programs Paid to: The Graduate Assembly (GA) or any university-recognized successor organization Purpose: To expand the GA’s budget,allowing the GA to offer more GRSO funding,employment opportunities for students,and student-initiated equity grants. Do you approve this fee?
